A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D. Corresponding material can be reliably matched despite revisions and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original model-training and IsoFLOP experiments, language-understanding evaluations, conditional-generation results, reversal experiments, and temporal-shift tests.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds evaluations of a more extensively trained MDM, GSM8K fine-tuning, T5 reversal experiments, and an additional guidance control.

M1.justification: The MDM architecture, masking and denoising processes, training objective, unsupervised CFG formulation, and Appendix A sampling algorithm remain unchanged. The replacement checkpoint and GSM8K experiments use existing methods with different training and evaluation settings.

E1.justification: v2 adds augmented mathematical-reasoning training data and GSM8K evaluation, extending coverage to supervised multi-step mathematical reasoning. The eight existing language-understanding benchmarks, ShareGPT/MT-Bench, reversal dataset, and FineWeb scenarios remain. ARC-e and Obqa are shortened names for retained benchmarks.

E2.justification: v2 Table 2 adds evaluated TinyLlama-1.1B and Llama-2-7B comparators to language understanding while retaining GPT-2. The 220M ARM comparisons in v1 Table 2 are removed rather than relocated. v2 Table 5 additionally evaluates T5-3B on reversal, alongside the retained GPT-3 and Llama-2-13B comparisons.

E3.justification: Appendices B.2–B.3 explicitly replace the language-understanding MDM trained for 1.6×10^21 FLOPs plus variable-length fine-tuning with one pretrained for 3.3×10^21 FLOPs using 1% variable-length data; batch size changes from 384 to 1024. New protocols include 40-epoch GSM8K fine-tuning and compute-matched CFG evaluation. Generation and reversal retain the earlier MDM.

E4.justification: New Appendix C.3/Table 13 tests whether CFG remains beneficial at equal sampling computation, comparing 128/256 guided steps with 256/512 unguided steps. Existing length-handling and likelihood-estimation ablations, scaling analysis, temporal tests, reversal CFG ablation, and generated examples are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions retain 128 Monte Carlo samples for validation-loss estimation and 1024 for the likelihood-method comparison. Neither reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests; v2 introduces no new statistical reporting practice.

E6.justification: The principal language-understanding results are replaced under changed training conditions: for example, MDM LAMBADA accuracy is 44.71 in v1 Table 3 and 52.73 in v2 Table 2. New results include GSM8K accuracy of 58.5 against a cited Llama-2 result of 58.6, T5 reversal scores, and an unguided 512-step MT-Bench score of 1.35. These additions do not establish same-setting improvements; existing scaling plots and generation/temporal results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(8), the scaling-law fitting formulation, and the conditional-distribution reasoning are unchanged. No mathematical definitions, formal assumptions, proofs, or derivations are substantively added or revised.

C1.justification: The headline empirical claims expand from beating GPT-2 on four benchmarks to beating it on six and matching TinyLlama's training budget while winning four benchmarks. v2 adds competitive GSM8K performance against Llama-2-7B using less than 5% of its pretraining FLOPs. Conversely, the conclusion narrows its broad comparable-or-superior performance claim and explicitly acknowledges scaling and generation gaps.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations linking chain-rule evaluation to stepwise reasoning and Monte Carlo evaluation to contextual understanding. Appendix C.4 explains T5's BLEU/exact-match discrepancy and attributes weaker reverse-direction MDM performance to greater train-test divergence. It also expands the training-objective explanation of reversal performance and removes v1's speculation about complementary ARM/MDM strengths.

D1.justification: Appendix B adds GSM8K training and sampling parameters, T5 learning-rate search details, and explicit documentation of which pretrained MDM serves each experiment. Table 7 adds model-checkpoint and mathematical-dataset links. Most existing reproducibility information remains, although v1's explicit 24-GPU pretraining count is dropped.

R1.justification: Section 3 now distinguishes its scaling-law study from Ye et al.'s earlier XLM-RoBERTa adaptation work. New Appendix C.1 positions unsupervised CFG relative to Zhao et al. and Holtzman et al.; mathematical-reasoning, T5, and reversal-explanation references are also added. These clarify positioning while retaining the central novelty claims.

P1.justification: v2 locally rewrites the abstract, introduction, language-understanding discussion, and conclusion. Section 5 loses the zero-shot qualifier, Appendix C gains a related-work subsection, and terminology and typographical errors are corrected. The overall section order and most explanatory text remain.

P2.justification: The two main language-understanding tables are replaced by one expanded table; the reversal table gains T5, and a new appendix ablation table is added. Resource and benchmark-example tables expand, with associated caption and placement changes. All six figures retain their substantive visual content.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation of central claims: Table 2 supplies a same-size, same-data, compute-matched TinyLlama comparison missing at the 1.1B scale in v1, and Table 13 addresses the extra-computation confound in CFG evaluation. GSM8K and T5 broaden capability testing, while clearer budget disclosures and a qualified conclusion improve interpretation. Removing the 220M comparison loses useful evidence, and uncertainty reporting remains absent, but the stronger controls and comparisons provide a substantial net improvement.
